title: Peach and Black Tea Barbecue Glaze
description: Soft peaches and mild black tea make a smooth, spoon-coating barbecue glaze with a small amount of tomato and cider vinegar.

ingredients.name: brewed unsweetened black tea
ingredients.note: Brew lightly; decaffeinated tea also works.

steps.title: Poach the peaches
steps.text: Place {peaches} and {tea} in the HexClad. Cover and simmer over medium-low for 8–10 minutes until a spoon easily crushes the fruit.

steps.title: Season the base
steps.text: Stir in {tomato}, {vinegar}, {sugar}, {aminos}, {paprika} and {onion}. Simmer gently for 2 minutes until the paste is fully incorporated.

steps.title: Puree the fruit
steps.text: Blend in a deep heatproof jug until smooth, then pass through a sieve back into the skillet. Aim for about 5 tablespoons of smooth base per serving.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Serve as a glaze
steps.text: Spoon the glaze over hot pulled pork or fold it into the pork juices just before serving. Reserve clean sauce for the table.

notes: Make ahead: Make the glaze a day ahead for the peach and tea flavors to blend. Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in small portions for up to 2 months. Whisk the fruit puree smooth when reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm in the HexClad over medium-low, stirring with a splash of water or broth if needed. Bring the whole sauce briefly to a rolling boil, then serve. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Whisk smooth and follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses tea, tomato and vinegar. For gentler Option B, replace the tea with water, replace the paste with smooth peach puree, omit the vinegar and use sweet unsmoked paprika.
